approaches.name: digital ESIA monitoring and GIS-based ministry information systems
approaches.description: The project builds a digital system to monitor environmental and social impact assessments and overhauls ministry M&E with GIS and natural capital satellite accounts. Practices: digital ESIA/ESMP monitoring system; GIS-based ministry information systems and natural capital satellite accounts.
approaches.why_innovative: New process: digital tracking of ESIA/ESMP compliance - cue: 'digital monitoring system' | category Technological; adoption apply; judged in 1 round(s); final check: digital core, in_use before 2019

evidence.text: This subcomponent will support: (a) strengthening management of E&S risks, including dissemination of a new Environment Code; preparation of related regulations and guidelines including on climate change risks and mitigation measures; development of an E&S management training program for key ministries, staff of the Project Implementation Units (PIUs), and young professionals; and development of a digital monitoring system for Environmental and Social Impact Assessments (ESIAs) and Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs) and (b) enhancement of environmental monitoring systems, including the management of environmental emergencies in the regions (technical assistance, training, equipment, and information systems) and the expansion of the air quality monitoring system.

extra_evidence.text: The project will also support the overhaul of the M&E systems of the two ministries, through support for the development and modernization of information systems (for example, geographic information system [GIS]-based systems), statistical databases (for example, natural capital satellite accounts), and related analytical products (for example, on value chains).
These systems will both reinforce the rationality of decision-making based on accurate and up-to-date information and increase transparency on natural resource capital and its management.

sector.rationale: Digital ESIA/ESMP monitoring is a cross-cutting public administration function, matching the largest sector share.

approaches.name: national forest monitoring, timber traceability and digital patrol systems
approaches.description: The project builds a national forest monitoring and traceability system using remote sensing, inventories and labeling, and equips forestry staff with drones, camera traps and digital patrol planning. Practices: national forest monitoring and timber traceability system; National forest monitoring system with remote sensing and inventories; Forest product traceability system for legal fuelwood and charcoal; Drones, camera traps and digital mission planning for forest patrols.
approaches.why_innovative: New service: national forest monitoring and timber traceability - cue: 'traceability' | category Technological; adoption apply; judged in 1 round(s); final check: digital core, in_use before 2019

evidence.text: (b) improving forest knowledge and monitoring (that is, technical assistance, training, and fieldwork to support a national forest monitoring system50 and a forest product traceability system); and (c) facilitating cooperation on illegal timber trade by building on the high-level dialogue initiated between Senegal and The Gambia (that is, regional study on illegal timber trade to identify measures to stop illegal cross-border timber trafficking and provide support to regional coordination meetings with relevant regional and international stakeholders).

extra_evidence.text: 49 Regulations of the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES), support systems for forest monitoring including the Mapping, Resource Assessment, and Information System Unit.

The project will support the following: • Planning and implementation of a national forest monitoring system to provide updated and accurate information on forest resources, management, and changes with technical assistance integrating data from national and local inventories, using mapping and remote sensing data, and establishing a coordination framework to ensure the monitoring of changes and trends over time.

However, Senegal needs to develop the required tools to (i) characterize and assess the national forest capital and monitor forest changes and GHG emissions resulting from land use change, deforestation, and forest degradation;

This system will integrate a measurement, reporting, and verification framework, in accordance with the UNFCCC104 guidelines, to monitor the NDC commitments in forests. • Setting up of a forest product traceability system to curb illegal logging and achieve the objective of fuelwood and charcoal supply coming systematically from sustainably managed forests, including through product labeling.
This system could be extended to forest products and will be developed with external technical assistance.
